correctness.rationale: The two-subset permutation character is \(\binom{X_1}{2}+X_2\). Its irreducible complement to the point permutation representation is indexed by \((n-2,2)\), with degree \(n(n-3)/2\), from the rank-three action. The character \(\binom{X_1}{2}+X_2-X_1\) has negative value \(-1\) precisely at \(X_1\in\{1,2\}\) and \(X_2=0\). Its mean vanishes, so its absolute mean is twice that permutation probability. The central idempotent convolution kernel has absolute row and column sums equal to degree times that mean, attained by a sign input; this proves sharp endpoint norms and equality classes. Counting the one or two fixed points gives the two-term formula involving permutations with no cycles of length one or two. The exact cycle-index EGF is \(e^{-z-z^2/2}/(1-z)\), yielding the limit. Exhaustive checks for \(4\le n\le8\), two independent recurrences, and exact small-group character convolution checks passed. Finite evidence is not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The first quadratic irreducible Specht block in the two-subset permutation action is a canonical Fourier projection on \(S_n\). Its sharp \(\ell^1\)/\(\ell^\infty\) amplification norm is a natural exact operator invariant; it is not supplied by the \(\ell^2\)-norm-one property or by the character polynomial alone without a global sign analysis. An all-rank count, all extremizers, and a nontrivial Poisson-cycle asymptotic have concrete potential use in filtering pairwise observables on permutations. This is an infinite natural family and not an arbitrary finite table or tiny numerical increment.
